title: Sukuma Wiki (Kenyan Collard Greens with Tomato and Ginger)
summary: Collard greens cut into thin ribbons and sautéed with browned onion, fresh tomato and matchsticks of ginger, cooked either crisp-tender or soft and dark.
equipment: large frying pan or sauté pan

ingredients.note: washed, stalks removed, leaves cut into 5 mm ribbons

ingredients.item: fresh ginger, peeled and cut into fine matchsticks
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Prepare the greens
steps.text: Swish the leaves in a large bowl of water to remove any grit and drain. Cut out the tough central stalks, then stack a few leaves, roll them tightly and slice into thin ribbons. Thin ribbons cook quickly and evenly.

steps.title: Cook the base
steps.text: Heat the oil in the pan over medium-high heat and cook the onion for 5 min until soft and lightly browned. Add the tomato, ginger and a pinch of the salt and cook for 5 min, stirring, until the tomatoes collapse.

steps.title: Add the greens
steps.text: Add the collards with the rest of the salt and toss well. Cook, lowering the heat if needed, for 8-10 min for bright, slightly crunchy greens or 15-25 min for soft, dark greens. Add the lemon juice if you like and serve.

tips: Kale or spring greens work instead of collards.
Add a crushed garlic clove or a pinch of chilli flakes with the tomatoes for a coastal-style version.
Serve with ugali, rice, chapati or grilled meat.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat in a pan until piping hot (74 °C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
